data.title: SA analyst sees record highs ahead despite tech selloff
data.description:
Wall Street ended lower Friday as technology stocks extended their losses, although Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research maintained a bullish outlook for equities through year-end.

King said investors heavily concentrated in high-beta artificial intelligence infrastructure stocks have faced significant losses, with several names falling at least 30% from their previous week's highs.

“This week there has been much pain inflicted on anyone overly concentrated in niche high-beta AI infrastructure stocks,” King stated, highlighting the risks of concentrated exposure to volatile technology investments. 

Despite the selloff, he argued that major equity benchmarks continue to display constructive technical patterns, suggesting the recent weakness has not undermined the broader market's upward trajectory. 

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) fell -0.3% Friday. The S&P 500 (SP500) declined -1.1%, while the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) plunged 2.1%.

King also noted that Treasury yields had declined considerably from the previous week, providing a potentially supportive backdrop for equities. 

“We continue to look to new ATHs into year end,” he said, maintaining his optimistic outlook despite mounting pressure on AI-related stocks.

data.title: U.S. equities tumbled lower and closed in the red as the tech selloff continued
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages finished deep in the red on Friday as technology stocks came under further pressure.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) closed -0.3%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) finished -1.1%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) ended -2.1%. 

From a sector-by-sector basis, six of the 11 segments concluded in the green, led by energy. At the other end of the spectrum, info tech struggled the most. 

A pullback in artificial intelligence-related stocks has weighed on the broader market this week, with memory chip stocks among the hardest-hit segments as investors reassessed the sector's recent performance. 

“This week there has been much pain inflicted on anyone overly concentrated in niche high-beta AI infrastructure stocks, many of which are down 30% or more from last week’s highs.  The equity indices though retain a bullish look in our view,” Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research stated.

On the economic calendar, industrial production growth accelerated more than expected in September. U.S. industrial production data  rose 0.7% M/M in September, versus the 0.4% forecasted level.

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) fell by 4 basis points to 4.71%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) ticked up 1 basis point to 5.08%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) added 1 basis point to 5.43%. 

“We think that investors should start thinking of a 5%+ 10-year Treasury yield as the new normal, not a brief aberration. For years, the Treasury enjoyed the luxury of having huge rate insensitive buyers, such as China, Japan, and the Fed, but those buyers are gone now and Treasuries have to offer competitive returns at a time when they are increasing supply due to the government’s profligate spending, which itself is giving creditors reason to require a higher rate of return,” Dennis Follmer of Montis Financial stated. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of Diamondback Energy (FANG) advanced +4.2%, while shares of CoreWeave (CRWV) fell -11.9%.

data.title: Avino Silver & Gold raised to Buy at Roth on valuation, La Preciosa potential
data.description:
Avino Silver & Gold (ASM) gained 2.9% in Friday's trading as Roth Capital upgraded the precious metals miner to Buy from Neutral with a $7 price target, saying the stock's recent pullback has created a value opportunity, while the potential for positive catalysts from its La Preciosa silver project in Mexico appears on the horizon.

In addition to the value opportunity, Roth analyst Joe Reagor noted Avino (ASM) is actively examining the possibility of building a standalone mill for La Preciosa and expects the company to release a financial study in the coming months outlining the plan and then provide a timeline for potential development.

For Q3, Avino (ASM) reported silver equivalent production of 582,836 oz, up slightly from the year-earlier quarter on a consolidated basis, while development production at La Preciosa increased 5% Q/Q to 105,867 silver equivalent oz, consisting of 91,411 silver oz and 166 gold oz; Reagor said the results were "mixed" relative to his expectations.

data.title: Air Canada, United to add routes, increase flight capacity in 2027
data.description:
Air Canada (ACDVF) and United Airlines (UAL) plan to expand their Canada-US networks next summer, adding new routes and increasing flight capacity under a transborder partnership that the carriers have agreed to renew, subject to regulatory approval.

Air Canada (ACDVF) will introduce service from Toronto to Louisville on April 28, 2027, followed by flights from Montreal to Indianapolis and Edmonton to Newark beginning June 1. It will also deploy larger Airbus A220 (EADSF) aircraft on its Edmonton-San Francisco route to increase capacity.

United (UAL) plans seasonal flights between Newark and St. John's, Newfoundland, and new services linking Denver with Ottawa and Quebec City. The carrier will also increase flights between Washington, D.C., and Quebec City and boost daily seats between Denver and Winnipeg by 65%.

The expansion builds on a joint business agreement established in 2022 that has enabled 20 new transborder routes, according to Air Canada (ACDVF). The partnership supports more than 1,200 connecting itineraries between Canada and the United States.

Air Canada (ACDVF) said an application seeking approval of the renewed and expanded agreement had been submitted to Transport Canada.

The carriers said the additional services would broaden travel options and improve connections through their respective networks. The announcement comes amid softer cross-border demand in recent months.

data.title: Wells Fargo wins court order to dismiss former CEO's pay-related case - report
data.description:
A San Francisco court has ruled in favor of Wells Fargo (WFC) to dismiss former CEO Tim Sloan's $34M lawsuit, Bloomberg News reported.

In a complaint filed in 2023, Sloan claimed WFC canceled several promised stock and bonus awards between 2015 and 2019, according to the report published on Friday.

Judge Christine Van Aken granted the bank's request to resolve the case without a trial, or at least narrow the claims, on the ground that Wells Fargo made the compensation decisions using its discretion in good faith, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: FMC downgraded at Jefferies as 'visibility deteriorates, again' with guidance cut
data.description:
FMC Corp. (FMC) rebounded 1.7% in Friday's trading after plunging 31% in the previous session when the agricultural chemicals company slashed its Q3 revenue guidance to $65M-$125M, far below consensus estimates, with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $510M-$565M, compared to its previous outlook for positive $120M-$140M.

Following the guidance cut, Jefferies analysts Daniel Rizzo and Charles Boakye downgraded FMC (FMC) shares to Hold from Buy with a new $5 price target, citing limited visibility, macro headwinds, and persistent pressure from generics.

The current crop protection market remains at a trough, and FMC (FMC) moved to reduce pricing on a wide range of off-patent crop protection products and simplify its North American pricing strategy, no longer using the high-gross margin, high-rebate model; as a result, the company cut its Q3 revenue and EBITDA projections, Rizzo and Boakye said.

Commodity pricing pressures will likely persist through the 2027 growing seasons, the analysts said, estimating a ~10% pricing decline next year in the core portfolio—offsetting 1%-2% volume growth—with rynaxypyr posing another $100M headwind.

On the positive side, new products including biologicals likely remain on track, and the benefits from the footprint optimization likely will be evident by H2 2027, according to Rizzo and Boakye, adding that Fluindapyr continues to ramp, and Dodhylex and Isoflex are positioned for significant growth beginning in 2028.

data.title: Travelers expects more than $3.6B fixed income net investment income in 2027, while raising cyber quota share cession
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: The Travelers Companies, Inc. (TRV) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "We're pleased to report excellent third quarter results" with "very strong underwriting performance across all 3 segments" and "a record result from our investment portfolio," and the company reported "core income of $1.95 billion or $9.18 per diluted share" and "core return on equity of 22.1%" (Chairman & CEO Alan Schnitzer).
  • "We generated net written premiums of $11.5 billion" as Business Insurance produced "net written premiums of $5.9 billion" ("4% higher than the prior year quarter, adjusting for the sale of our Canadian business"), Bond & Specialty "grew net written premiums by 12% to $1.2 billion," and Personal Insurance generated "net written premiums of $4.4 billion" (CEO Schnitzer).
  • "We returned $1.8 billion of excess capital to shareholders during the quarter, including $1.5 billion of share repurchases" and "just since the beginning of 2025, we have returned $8 billion in capital through share repurchases, retiring 12% of the shares then outstanding" (CEO Schnitzer).
  • "For unrepresented claimants, we've developed a digital tool to help resolve claims promptly and fairly" and "when a claimant has an attorney, we're using AI to sharpen our responses to their demands" as Travelers emphasized its effort to "bend the loss cost curve" tied to "legal system abuse" (CEO Schnitzer).
  • "For the first time ever, after-tax net investment income surpassed $900 million for the quarter" and the company noted the rate-driven mark-to-market impact: "the significant increase in interest rates during the quarter resulted in an increase in our net unrealized investment loss from $2 billion after tax at June 30 to $6.4 billion after tax at September 30" (Executive VP & CFO Daniel Frey).

Outlook

  • "Our outlook for fixed income NII in the fourth quarter, including earnings from short-term securities, is up slightly from the outlook we provided a quarter ago, now expecting approximately $875 million after tax in Q4, bringing the full year 2026 total to $3.3 billion" (CFO Frey).
  • "For 2027, we expect more than $3.6 billion, with quarterly figures starting at around $875 million in Q1 and growing to around $965 million in Q4" (CFO Frey).
  • "Effective October 1, we increased the percentage ceded to our cyber reinsurance quota share" which "will reduce net written premiums by about $165 million in Q4 and by about $230 million for full year 2027" and Travelers said, "We expect the impact on bottom line earnings to be de minimis in both years" (CFO Frey).
  • Compared with Q2, Travelers updated the fixed income NII path by lifting Q3 actuals versus its prior "expecting approximately $840 million in the third quarter" view and stated Q4 is now "up slightly" (CFO Frey, Q2 and Q3 calls).

Financial Results

  • Travelers reported "underwriting income of $1.4 billion pretax" and "total net favorable development of $234 million pretax" while "catastrophe losses in the quarter were $538 million pretax" (CFO Frey).
  • Business Insurance delivered "record third quarter segment income of $1.04 billion" with "a combined ratio that improved 2 points to a terrific 90.9%" and "underlying combined ratio... 88.9%" while "net written premium reached a third quarter record at $5.9 billion" (Executive VP & President of Business Insurance Greg Toczydlowski).
  • Bond & Specialty posted "record segment income of $309 million" and "a terrific combined ratio of 77.3%" while reporting "net written premiums... 12%... to $1.2 billion" and "Surety... net written premium growth of 21%" (Executive VP & President of Bond & Specialty Insurance Jeffrey Klenk).
  • Personal Insurance delivered "segment income of $706 million" and "combined ratio of 83.5%" with "underlying combined ratio of 76.7%"; Auto posted "combined ratio of 87.1%" and management flagged seasonality: "the fourth quarter Auto underlying loss ratio has historically been about 5 to 6 points above the average for the first 3 quarters" (Executive VP & President of Personal Insurance Michael Klein).

Q&A

  • David Motemaden, Evercore ISI: asked about "the durability" of underlying underwriting income; Chairman & CEO Schnitzer: "We would absolutely reiterate the durability of underlying underwriting income" and CFO Frey: "the ZIP code that we're in now is just a completely different ZIP code than we used to be in."
  • David Motemaden, Evercore ISI: asked if BI favorable PYD included GL; CFO Frey: "It was all lines across the board... including GL."
  • Charles Peters, Raymond James: asked if management was "foreshadowing another negative step change" in casualty loss cost trend; CEO Schnitzer: "No, quite the contrary... it's as we've expected. No surprises at all."
  • Charles Peters, Raymond James: asked about AI initiatives like "Muse" and distribution; President Klein: "it's early days" and cited adoption, data, and "legal and regulatory considerations"; CEO Schnitzer: digital trading is "way over at the simplest end" today.
  • Joshua Shanker, BofA: asked whether tech savings could be redeployed into pricing; CEO Schnitzer: "we are generating operating leverage" and "if we decide that we want to redeploy some of those into pricing without compromising our return objectives, we'll do that."
  • Michael Zaremski, BMO: asked about the downward trend in commercial RPC; CEO Schnitzer: "If there's one word over the top to describe it, I would say it's stable" and called liability line sequential movement "modest."
  • Elyse Greenspan, Wells Fargo: asked about expense ratio stability into 2027; CFO Frey: "we'll decide what we want the expense ratio to be and then dial into that number" and guided to being "pretty copacetic" with current levels.
  • Andrew Kligerman, TD Cowen: asked about personal lines competition; President Klein: "we're definitely not one to chase premium growth at all costs" and emphasized matching "price to risk" plus distribution actions including "book consolidation opportunities."
  • Yaron Kinar, Mizuho: asked about cyber viability amid AI; President Klenk: limits are "a substantial majority... at $1 million or less" and cyber is "one of our most heavily reinsured lines of business"; CEO Schnitzer on backstop: "I don't really know."
  • Matthew Heimermann, Citi: asked about claims-practices scrutiny; President Klein: comparisons of close-without-pay are "very fragile" and practices are grounded in "pay what we owe"; CEO Schnitzer: the company is "very attentive to this" and "very engaged in speaking to it."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly skeptical, with repeated probing on reserve releases, loss trend/"step change," growth vs. margins, distribution disruption ("spooking the market"), cyber systemic risk, and regulatory scrutiny.
  • Management: positive and confident in prepared remarks ("tremendous confidence") and generally firm in Q&A, using clarifiers like "No, quite the contrary" (CEO Schnitzer) and "We certainly have not run to the other side of the boat" (CFO Frey).
  • Versus Q2, the tone remained confident; Q3 added more defense of claims practices and more explicit discussion of AI-driven distribution change ("it's early days") while maintaining the "stable" pricing framing.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 emphasized litigation/social inflation countermeasures and AI in claims as a central strategic message, while Q2 centered on explaining the broader "earnings engine" and "Innovation 2.0" (CEO Schnitzer, Q2 and Q3 calls).
  • Investment income became more forward-defined in Q3, adding explicit 2027 fixed income NII expectations ("more than $3.6 billion") versus Q2’s guidance focused on 2026 quarterly outlook.
  • Capital return stayed prominent in both quarters; Q3 highlighted "$1.8 billion" returned in-quarter and cumulative "$8 billion" since early 2025, while Q2 discussed authorization capacity and capital philosophy.
  • Analyst focus shifted from Q2’s ROE/capital return and BI competitive dynamics toward Q3’s reserve accident-year granularity, AI distribution (Muse), and claims-regulatory scrutiny.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Lawsuit abuse" and "upward pressure on liability losses" remained a stated risk, with Travelers positioning mitigation through "technology" and willingness to "defend our customers in litigation" (CEO Schnitzer).
  • Interest-rate volatility was highlighted via the unrealized loss swing to "$6.4 billion after tax"; management stressed it is "interest rate driven, not credit quality driven" and said the same rate move is "a tailwind for future results" (CFO Frey).
  • Cyber exposure was framed as "a dynamic exposure" with AI increasing that dynamic; management cited limits management, heavy reinsurance, and risk control investments (President Klenk).

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as another quarter of strong underwriting across all segments alongside record investment income, paired with substantial shareholder capital return. Executives highlighted a more explicit multi-quarter investment income outlook into 2027, a cyber quota share cession that reduces reported premiums with "de minimis" earnings impact, and expanded commentary on using AI and claims strategy to counter litigation-driven loss pressure, while repeatedly characterizing pricing conditions as "stable" and reserve positioning as disciplined.

data.title: What's next for Chinese EV competition?
data.description:
Investors Should Know: The global electric vehicle industry is entering a new phase of competition. Consumers are looking at price, as well as factors like premium branding, shared infrastructure, and embedded digital services. These could provide alternative paths for differentiation and margin protection.

Key Takeaways

  • Aggressive promotions and lower-priced vehicles are intensifying margin pressure across the Chinese EV market, pushing manufacturers to find competitive advantages beyond volume.
  • Premiumization is emerging as one response to price competition, with higher average selling prices offering a potential buffer against discounting dynamics in mass-market segments.
  • Battery-swapping infrastructure partnerships represent a cooperative approach to scaling EV adoption, allowing manufacturers to share development costs rather than build independently.
  • Software and connected-car services are becoming part of the vehicle value proposition, pointing toward a future where digital integration supplements hardware as a differentiator.
  • Proposed EU import restrictions on Chinese hybrid vehicles introduce a policy variable that could reshape competitive dynamics in Europe, with implications for both Chinese and European automakers.

Background: How EV Automakers Are Competing Beyond Price

The electric vehicle industry in China is experiencing a period of intense price competition. Manufacturers across the market are relying on promotions to sustain delivery growth, which compresses margins even when unit volumes are rising. That environment is pushing automakers to identify differentiation strategies that do not depend on undercutting rivals on sticker price.

Three strategic responses are visible in the current landscape. Premium brand positioning targets buyers less sensitive to price. Shared charging and battery-swapping infrastructure reduces the per-company cost of building the network that makes EV ownership practical. Embedded software services add a recurring or integrated digital layer to what has historically been a hardware-only product. Each approach addresses a different dimension of the ownership proposition.

Stocks to Watch

Geely Automobile Holdings (GELYF) is a Chinese automaker pursuing a multi-brand strategy that spans mass-market and premium electric vehicles, with an international expansion program and a growing focus on software integration. Its ZEEKR brand sits at the premium end of its EV portfolio.

Broader publicly traded names across the EV and autonomous mobility space include Pony AI Inc. (PONY), ChargePoint Holdings, Inc. (CHPT), EVgo, Inc. (EVGO), QuantumScape Corporation (QS), Microvast Holdings, Inc. (MVST), Solid Power, Inc. (SLDP), SES AI Corporation (SES), Enovix Corporation (ENVX), Amprius Technologies, Inc. (AMPX), and Electrovaya Inc. (ELVA).

On the global automobile manufacturing side, Honda Motor Co., Ltd. (HMC), Ford Motor Company (F), General Motors Company (GM), Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG (DRPRY), and Nissan Motor Co., Ltd. (NSANY) are among the major publicly traded names currently carrying Buy or Strong Buy Quant Ratings. Tesla (TSLA) also remains a major name in the global EV industry.

News Roundup

  • Geely's ZEEKR premium EV brand nearly doubled first-half 2026 sales volume to 178,000 units, with brand-specific revenue exceeding RMB 55 billion, alongside a 30% investment in NIO's battery-swapping subsidiary to share infrastructure development costs.
  • Geely Holding announced plans to integrate Google in-car services, including Gemini, Play, and Maps, across its overseas vehicle brands starting in the second half of 2027, subject to regulatory approval.
  • The European Union was reported to be considering an annual cap of 350,000 Chinese hybrid-vehicle imports, with potential measures beginning December 1, a development that could limit Chinese automaker expansion in Europe while offering some relief to European manufacturers.
  • Lithium carbonate futures in China fell sharply following the EU-China trade developments, with expectations that lithium markets could move from deficit toward balance and then surplus over the following two years, adding uncertainty to battery input cost projections.

data.title: Softbank falls amid report it's evaluating bid for US security firm Allied
data.description:
Softbank (SFTBY) dropped 9.5% amid a report that the company is considering a purchase of Allied Universal, the largest security services firm in the US.

A potential deal may value closely held Allied at an equity value of as much as $18 billion, according to a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

Deliberations are preliminary, and no final decisions have been made, including on a possible price, the people told Bloomberg,

The security company, which is backed by private equity firm Warburg Pincus and Canadian pension fund La Caisse, has about $12 billion in publicly traded debt, which could bring a total value for a transaction to around $30 billion.

Representatives for SoftBank, Warburg Pincus, and La Caisse declined to comment to Bloomberg. An Allied spokesperson didn’t respond to requests for comment.

data.title: WaFd outlines EverBank deal economics with 29% EPS accretion target and first calendar quarter 2027 close timeline
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: WaFd (WAFD) Q4 2026

Management view

  • “We closed out our fiscal year 2026 on a high note with earnings per share up 22% over the prior year.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Brent Beardall)

  • “In what is likely to be our final fiscal year before we merge with EverBank, we are proud to deliver our second best year ever in terms of after-tax net income of $241 million.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

  • “WaFd Inc. reported net income available to common shareholders of $56.3 million or $0.76 per diluted share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.” (Executive VP & CFO Kelli Holz)

  • “The company sold $543 million of single-family residential loans during the quarter and has entered into an agreement to sell $429 million of multifamily loans in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Absent any changes in interest rates, we expect our margin to expand modestly over the next quarter or 2 with the reduction in earning assets due to the loan sales in addition to our earning assets repricing more quickly than our liabilities in the short term in a rising rate environment.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Ultimately, this relationship resulted in a large impairment well outside of our historical loss results.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Ryan Mauer)

  • “Our previously announced expected closing time frame of the first calendar quarter 2027 remains on track.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

  • “With all of that for context, the question I receive most often now is why did WaFd decide to partner with EverBank?” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

  • “Our pro forma bank… shows that with a 3% margin… we can achieve just shy of a 15% return on tangible common equity.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

  • “Through this merger, we will be able to fair value the WaFd balance sheet, including the $6.6 billion of single-family residential loans that are today earning only 4.25% and mark those loans to market rates.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

  • “We were able to do it with the following metrics: 9.8% pro forma CET1 at close, only 8% dilution to WaFd existing shareholders and 29% EPS accretion to WaFd shareholders once the cost saves are fully realized.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

Outlook

  • No analyst-estimate comparison was included because the provided estimates tag did not contain a valid fiscalQuarter format.

  • “Absent any changes in interest rates, we expect our margin to expand modestly over the next quarter or 2.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Earlier this month, we filed our regulatory applications, and we expect to file our proxy within the next 2 weeks.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

  • “Our previously announced expected closing time frame of the first calendar quarter 2027 remains on track.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

Financial results

  • No analyst-estimate comparison was included because the provided estimates tag did not contain a valid fiscalQuarter format.

  • “WaFd Inc. reported net income available to common shareholders of $56.3 million or $0.76 per diluted share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026… and $0.84 per share for the June 2026 quarter.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Loans receivable decreased $977 million during the quarter as a result of the loan sale-related activity.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “We expect to realize a net gain of approximately $7 million when this sale is finalized.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Total deposits increased by $389 million during the quarter… Core deposits ended the quarter at 81.8% compared to the June quarter at 80.6% of total deposits.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “The net interest margin held steady at 2.81%, no change from the June 30, 2026 quarter.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Total noninterest income was $38.1 million for the September 2026 quarter compared to $24.2 million for the prior quarter… primarily driven by a $16.4 million gain on the sale of single-family loans during the quarter.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “Total noninterest expense was $121.5 million compared to $110.3 million for the June quarter… combined with $6.2 million in merger-related costs incurred in the fourth quarter.” (Executive VP & CFO Holz)

  • “$39.2 million of net charge-offs were taken during the quarter, inclusive of the problem loan mentioned previously.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Mauer)

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts were slightly negative to pressing on near-term profitability mechanics around loan-sale-driven earning asset declines and expense run-rate, including “Loans are going to be down roughly $1 billion” (Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler & Co., Research Division) and “as we think about… how much is going to be used to pay down borrowings versus reinvestment” (Kelly Motta, Keefe, Bruyette, & Woods, Inc., Research Division).

  • Management tone in prepared remarks was positive and strategic on the EverBank rationale and pro forma targets, including “this is a game changer” and “29% EPS accretion” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Brent Beardall), while Q&A responses were more guarded on near-term actions, including “we haven't made definitive plans, nothing to announce” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall).

  • Versus the prior quarter, prepared-remark tone shifted from highlighting share-price strength (“we were pleased to see the stock provide a 23% total shareholder return for the quarter”) (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall, Q3) to acknowledging market pushback on the announced deal (“Since we announced our deal, our stock is down 18.9%… roughly a 10% delta.”) (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall, Q4).

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Guidance language on margin shifted from “we expect our margin to be relatively flat for the next quarter” (Executive VP & CFO Kelli Holz, Q3) to “we expect our margin to expand modestly over the next quarter or 2” (Executive VP & CFO Holz, Q4).

  • Credit narrative shifted from a pending resolution to a realized loss: “Outstanding balances for this relationship amounts to $54 million… with anticipated sale of the business” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Ryan Mauer, Q3) versus “this relationship resulted in a large impairment” and “$39.2 million of net charge-offs” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Mauer, Q4).

  • Capital and buyback discussion moved from flexibility (“We will continue to be opportunistic with our share repurchases”) (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Brent Beardall, Q3) to constraint (“we're not in a position to be buying back shares today”) (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall, Q4).

  • Strategy emphasis broadened from Build 2030 execution and organic loan/deposit growth (Q3) to a merger-led business model shift: “we are changing our business model so that we are not solely reliant on noninterest-bearing deposit growth to hit our return goals” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall, Q4).

Risks and concerns

  • “This loss was significant for the bank and is well outside of our normalized loss history.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Ryan Mauer)

  • “The economic uncertainty driven by continued inflationary pressures, energy supply shocks driven by the war in the Middle East and tariffs will continue to impact the borrowers' top line revenue results as well as operating costs.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Mauer)

  • “All of this is, of course, pending receipt of the requisite approvals from both shareholders and regulators.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Brent Beardall)

  • “You cannot argue with the market.” (President, CEO & Vice Chairman Beardall)

Final takeaway

Management framed Q4 as a quarter with steady margin, higher noninterest income from loan sales, and elevated credit costs tied to a single large C&I impairment, while emphasizing merger economics and timing for the EverBank transaction, including a first calendar quarter 2027 close expectation and pro forma targets such as “29% EPS accretion” and “just shy of a 15% return on tangible common equity” under a “3% margin” scenario.
